# Assessment clarification after candidate inspection

The counting/alignment policy was saved before any candidate outputs were inspected. It provides an ambiguity safeguard but names only `alignment_ambiguous`. One encountered case is different: the selected Beklemishev footnote is geometrically and textually aligned without ambiguity, but its role is explicit only in the Docling node's `label: footnote`. Saved markdown and chunks flatten raised `1` to baseline `1` and merge the footnote with body prose without an explicit footnote-role field.

The comparison therefore adds the status `fidelity_indeterminate` for this one case. This is a disclosed assessment refinement, not a frozen-label change or a replacement selection. The number is retained and no scientific exponent is invented; no claim of a false scientific repair is made. Conversely, structural Docling evidence is not silently treated as proof that a plain-text reader receives an explicit footnote marker. Both lower and upper fidelity/recall bounds retain this case in their denominator. Docling semantic role preservation is judged faithful because the aligned node explicitly remains a footnote.

Recorded source-page-selection exclusions are more specific than the predeclared general `excluded_by_surface_policy`: source pages outside consumed `keeppages` never enter extraction. They are reported separately and included in the all-source occurrence coverage denominator. A second, clearly conditional denominator covers only included source pages. Neither denominator is called repair precision.
